scenario: The Pandera does what it always does — the GC group settles it
note: The base case. Two kilometres of double-digit gradient from 4.5 km to go, a 15% ramp at the flamme rouge and 40°C is as selective an ending as this race has, and unlike Calar Alto there is no irregular upper half to let dropped riders return — only a few hundred metres of dip and rise right at the top. References are hard Grand Tour and WT mountain days won by a GC leader from a group of two (mountain 0.41-0.49 over rolling): Pogacar's Peyragudes 2022, Vingegaard's TdF 2024 stage 11, Roglic's Angliru 2023, Almeida's Vuelta 2025 stage 13, Roglic's Dauphine 2024 stage 7. Inherits the config-root day key. Note the oracle's second route to gc_day — the front-5 median inside the morning top-10 — fires here even if a breakaway rider wins, provided the GC men fill the places behind him, which on a climb this steep is the likely shape.
